title: RG 330: Research and Development Board finding aids, 1946–1953

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: RG 330: Research and Development Board finding aids, 1946–1953
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Existing finding aids and archival control records describing
Research and Development Board records within Record Group 330,
Records of the Office of the Secretary of Defense, for any portion
of January 1, 1946, through December 31, 1953.

Please route this request to the reference/access staff responsible
for these RG 330 holdings and, as appropriate, the office responsible
for FOIA processing.

Please provide existing inventories, series descriptions, entry
lists, box and folder lists, file-classification guides, and subject
or project indexes for these holdings described in section 330.11.3
of NARA's Guide to Federal Records:

1. Records concerning fiscal and budgetary aspects of research and
development programs, described as covering 1946–1953.

2. Executive Council meeting minutes, described as covering
1946–1950.

3. Committee on Technical Information records, described as covering
1946–1953.

Please include existing indexes or registers identifying research
projects or studies represented in these specific holdings, together
with any accompanying keys or guides needed to interpret their
file codes.

The date range applies to the underlying historical records, not
to when the finding aids were prepared. Existing aids spanning
additional years may be supplied without creating a new version.

This request seeks existing descriptive and indexing records,
not copies of all underlying program files, minutes, or technical
reports and not the creation of a new research-project inventory.

Please include archival identifiers and access-restriction
information already contained in the requested aids.

If the materials are openly available, please provide them through
ordinary reference access or supply direct links to the specific
aids. Please process remaining restricted responsive records under
FOIA as applicable.

Please release reasonably segregable nonexempt portions and identify
any exemptions applied. Electronic delivery through MuckRock is
preferred. I authorize fees up to $25 total for this request; please
obtain my written approval before exceeding that amount. Contact me
to discuss any necessary clarification or narrowing.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Golden Plasma

title: RG 273: Einstein communications with Sidney Souers and Allen Dulles

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: RG 273: Einstein communications with Sidney Souers and Allen Dulles
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Federal-agency records in NARA's legal custody within Record Group
273, Records of the National Security Council, documenting either
of the following:

1. Communications or proposed or completed meetings between Albert
Einstein and Sidney William Souers, also identified as Sidney W.
Souers, in records originally created between January 1, 1947,
and April 18, 1955.

2. Communications or proposed or completed meetings between Albert
Einstein and Allen Welsh Dulles, also identified as Allen W. Dulles,
in records originally created between January 1, 1950, and
April 18, 1955.

Please route this request to the staff responsible for access to
RG 273 archival records.

Please include correspondence, retained drafts, enclosures,
memoranda of conversation, telephone memoranda, meeting notes,
and records arranging or acknowledging these communications or
meetings. Include communications transmitted on the individuals'
behalf by their secretaries, assistants, or other intermediaries,
and associated routing or correspondence-register entries.

Relevant locations include the Office of the Executive Secretary's
general correspondence, agency information files, and senior staff
files, as described in section 273.3 of NARA's Guide to Federal
Records, and related Secretariat or staff meeting records.

A record meeting either numbered category is responsive; all three
individuals need not appear together. Responsive records need not
mention "Project Jehovah" or any other project name.

This is not a request for every record mentioning these individuals.
It concerns their communications and contacts and includes later
reproductions of responsive historical records.

This request concerns federal-agency records, not donated
presidential or personal papers.

If further archival identifiers are necessary, please contact me
to clarify the scope. For responsive documents withheld from an
otherwise accessible file, please provide any releasable existing
withdrawal sheets or document identification records.

Please release reasonably segregable nonexempt portions and identify
any exemptions applied. Electronic delivery through MuckRock is
preferred. I authorize fees up to $25 total for this request; please
obtain my written approval before exceeding that amount. Contact me
to discuss any necessary clarification or narrowing.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Golden Plasma

title: Administrative records for F-2018-01827 and F-2018-01132

communications.subject: Freedom of Information Act Request: Administrative records for F-2018-01827 and F-2018-01132
communications.communication:
To Whom It May Concern:

Pursuant to the Freedom of Information Act, I hereby request the following records:

Existing administrative records for CIA FOIA cases F-2018-01827
and F-2018-01132, including associated administrative appeals and
Mandatory Declassification Review proceedings, if any, from the
opening of each case through the date of your search.

LOCATING INFORMATION

CIA released document C06849974, bearing an approval-for-release
date of April 14, 2023, contains a February 14, 2020, letter from
Timothy S. Cooper to the Agency Release Panel, stamped received
February 24, 2020.

Page 1 contains a typed reference to F-2018-01827, a handwritten
reference to F-2018-01132 in the upper-right corner, and a
handwritten "1132" beside the typed reference.

The letter refers to a March 2, 2018, FOIA request, a January 23,
2020, agency response, and four accompanying documents. It
describes the requested subject as General Smith's December 19,
1952, "Weekly Friday Black Book Briefing" to President Truman.

These details are provided to locate the administrative records.
I am not asserting that the two case numbers concern the same
subject or that the historical claims in the letter are correct.

RECORDS REQUESTED

1. For each case: the original request and attachments;
acknowledgments; scope-clarification correspondence; interim and
final responses; determination letters; and existing case-status
and tracking records.

2. Existing search taskings, component responses, search
descriptions, search-result summaries, referral or consultation
records, and processing notes retained in each administrative
case file.

3. Associated administrative appeals and MDR submissions, together
with agency acknowledgments, routing or referral records,
determinations, and dispositions, including those assigned
different tracking numbers.

4. Copies of records released in response to either case or its
associated proceedings, including the January 23, 2020, response
and the four documents described in the February 14, 2020, letter,
under whichever case or proceeding they were maintained.

5. Existing correspondence, annotations, routing records, case
cross-references, or tracking-system entries documenting any
correction, reassignment, renumbering, or other relationship
between F-2018-01827 and F-2018-01132, including the handling and
case assignment of the February 14, 2020, letter.

6. Any existing document lists, release indexes, or withholding
inventories retained in those administrative files. If either
file was transferred or disposed of, please include existing
transfer or disposition documentation in surviving administrative
records.

SCOPE AND DELIVERY

This is a new FOIA request for existing administrative records.
It is not an appeal of the earlier requester's determination,
a new MDR request, or a request to repeat the underlying
historical searches.

I already possess the released version of C06849974. Please do
not limit the response to that document or provide another
identical copy. Exact duplicates elsewhere in the responsive
records need be supplied only once; please retain existing case
labels and cross-references.

If records for one case are ready before the other, rolling
releases are welcome. For records already available online,
specific document identifiers and direct locations are acceptable.

I do not seek the prior requester's personal contact information,
identity-verification documents, payment information, or
handwritten signature. Please redact that information rather
than withholding otherwise responsive records in full.

The requested documents will be made available to the general public, and this request is not being made for commercial purposes.

In the event that there are fees, I would be grateful if you would inform me of the total charges in advance of fulfilling my request. I would prefer the request filled electronically, by e-mail attachment if available or CD-ROM if not.

Thank you in advance for your anticipated cooperation in this matter. I look forward to receiving your response to this request within 20 business days, as the statute requires.

Sincerely,

Golden Plasma
